answer: Admission is a measured thread, not a headcount. An applicant locks 15.8 POA and roots a living vine at a seed-drawn peg on a public island, then extends that vine along a 31-knot thread, one knot every 5 blocks, each knot an 8-byte live signature. Surveyors recompute the thread from the first peg; a skipped knot or a second vine on the same peg burns the 15.8 POA and bars those keys for seven epochs. Forging 2,200 identities needs 68,200 exclusive knots and 2,200 vine roots. If two threads share a preimage, both stakes slash at once.
